Pebble Makes Things Right After Owners Go Public With Disastrous 1-Year Experience With Pebble Flow
87 photos
Photo: Pebble RV
There are two sides to every story, and Pebble RV, a California-based startup promising "the trailer of tomorrow" with the futuristic, all-electric, self-driving Pebble RV, would like the chance to tell theirs before you make up your mind on the quality of the build of that trailer. They know they messed up, they say.
A story broke last weekend, when Ryan and Celeste, owners of a Pebble Flow travel trailer went on the record with their nightmarish one-year experience. They claimed the trailer was sub-par in terms of quality, construction, and functionality, and that bad customer service delayed their registration of the unit and effectively barred them from using it before it stuff started to fall apart.
It was a damning expose, and the two did on camera for RV consumer advocate Liz Amazing and her YouTube channel, backing their story with photos confirming issues encountered and fails that had appeared on the unit in storage. It was bad enough that all these were happening on a new unit , but it seemed even more so that it happened on a unit they did not use once camping.
Cracked fiberglass, cracked weather seals, a warped rear window, a solar panel lost on the way, a stabilizer foot pad lost the same way, and issues with the charger and the Two Assist system were just some of the issues Ryan and Celeste mentioned.
Photo: Pebble RV At the time the video was published, Pebble was yet to go on the record, even though commenters had already started pestering them with messages urging them to buy back the lemon from the couple.
Pebble RV took its time to respond to Ryan and Celeste's story, but what they say will probably make up for that. They recognize and accept the couple's version of the story, admitting that this first unit "did not meet their expectations or the standards we set for ourselves." They're also saying they have been in touch with the couple and will be buying back the faulty unit .
Pebble also adds some context.
Photo: YouTube/Liz Amazing The company says that, when the video was published, they had resolved all but two warranty repairs reported by the couple, both of which had been reported that same week. They own up to having delayed the registration of the trailer, they apologize for it.
Pebble also says that, earlier in 2026, they voluntarily recalled 22 units of the Pebble Flow after a single report of a detached solar panel, but they don't say whether it was this particular unit . Of these recalled units, 21 have already been repaired and returned, and one is still pending retrieval.
Pebble also mentions that, since the Founders Edition Pebble Flow went into production, which is what Ryan and Celeste bought in November 2025 for $190,000, they have implemented over "300 design and manufacturing improvements" into what is now Gen2 2027 Pebble Flow. The implication seems to be that these erase many of the faults noticed by the couple in their early version .
Photo: YouTube/Liz Amazing "Ryan was candid with me about what went wrong, and I'm grateful for that," Bingrui Yang, Pebble founder and CEO, says in the statement, assuring existing customers and pre-order holders that "we'll keep working until every owner has the experience we set out to build."
Ryan and Celeste's full story is at this link , but also in the second video at the bottom of the page.
